result.rule: When the description names an external party, such as another organization, a remote service, or a user-facing system, that exchanges messages with the process while the process runs: Model each such external party as its own pool, not as a lane inside the process's pool. Show the exchanges with it as message flows between the pools: from the process's sending tasks to the external pool, and from the external pool to the process's receiving events or tasks. Do not draw these exchanges as sequence flows, and do not place the external party in a lane of the process pool.

When The description says an outside party, after receiving a request from the process, performs one or more processing steps of its own, possibly choosing a branch itself (for example announcing a delay before a further step), and then sends replies back to the process.: Model the outside party as its own bpmn:participant pool with its own start and end events. Put each of its described processing steps there as a bpmn:task, in the order the description gives, and show any branch the party chooses itself as an exclusive gateway inside its pool. Connect the requesting process to that pool with message flows: the request crosses to the party, and each notice or reply it sends crosses back. In the requesting process, keep the send of the request and an intermediate catch event for each awaited reply or notice, then add an exclusive gateway where the description says the process branches on which message arrived. Do not replace the party's own processing steps with catch events in the requesting process.

When the description says the organization sends a request or case to an outside party and then waits for a reply from that party (such as a payment or an objection) that is received by the organization, without describing that party's own behaviour: Model the wait for the reply as an intermediate catch event in the organization's own process, placed after the request or case has been sent. Do not create a separate pool for the outside party, and do not add a message flow from the sending task to that party or from that party to the catch event.

When the description says that the party sends a request or material to another party and then has to wait for that party's reply, confirmation or status before it continues: Model the send as a send activity, and model the wait for the reply as an explicit receive activity placed directly after it and before the next activity or decision that depends on the reply. Do not connect the send activity directly to the later step, and do not drop the wait from the flow.

args.text: The description says the process sends an order to several outside parties (stores or friends) and later receives deliveries or replies from them, while the process keeps running; model each outside party as its own pool, with message flows from the sending task to that pool and from that pool to the catch event that waits for the delivery.

result.rule: Direct each message flow from sender to receiver. Its endpoints must belong to different pools and be valid interaction nodes.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
